text.arabic_uthmani: وَقَالَ يَٰبَنِىَّ لَا تَدْخُلُوا۟ مِنۢ بَابٍۢ وَٰحِدٍۢ وَٱدْخُلُوا۟ مِنْ أَبْوَٰبٍۢ مُّتَفَرِّقَةٍۢ ۖ وَمَآ أُغْنِى عَنكُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ مِن شَىْءٍ ۖ إِنِ ٱلْحُكْمُ إِلَّا لِلَّهِ ۖ عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ ۖ وَعَلَيْهِ فَلْيَتَوَكَّلِ ٱلْمُتَوَكِّلُونَ

words.gloss_range: resumptive coordinator opening continued speech
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) resumes the scene from 12:66: the counsel about gates begins as continued speech after the oath, not as a detached proverb. The particle keeps practical instruction, agency-disclaimer, and trust declaration inside one ongoing father-to-sons exchange.

topics.headline: resumptive speech continuation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah continues the oath-scene dialogue instead of opening a detached maxim.
topics.reason: The opening coordinator attaches the new saying to the prior witnessed speech frame in 12:66.

words.gloss_range: perfect speech verb introducing direct quoted counsel
words.root_gloss_range: speech, saying, reported declaration, and adopted stance; here the perfect verb frames Yaqub’s delivered counsel
words.prose: {{ar:قَالَ}} ({{tr:qāla}}) seals the whole counsel as Yaqub’s completed reported speech before the quotation unfolds. It is not neutral narration: the verb opens a five-beat utterance of prohibition, corrective command, inability-disclaimer, sovereignty restriction, and trust climax, while also joining same-surah father-address scenes (12:5; 12:87).

topics.headline: completed father-speech frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears the prohibition, command, disclaimer, sovereignty claim, and trust exhortation as one delivered father-speech.
topics.reason: The perfect speech verb governs the quoted unit and anchors the addressee structure before the commands.

words.gloss_range: vocative particle launching direct address
words.prose: {{ar:يَا}} ({{tr:yā}}) moves the report into direct address. It summons the sons before any command appears, so the gate strategy and the theological limit are heard interpersonally, as counsel spoken to them.

topics.headline: direct filial address
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the counsel is aimed directly at the sons, not stated as abstract travel advice.
topics.reason: The vocative particle immediately governs the filial address and shifts from narrator report into direct speech.

words.gloss_range: vocative plural filial address with first-person possessive force
words.root_gloss_range: sonship and derived relation, with a broader building/formation field; here the selected sense is filial address, while the structural-continuity image remains secondary
words.prose: {{ar:بَنِيَّ}} ({{tr:baniyya}}) makes the addressees Yaqub’s own sons, not anonymous travelers. The first-person possessive is felt inside the vocative, and the doubled yāʾ gives the address heightened affection rather than a bare kinship label; the broader {{ar:ب ن ي}} ({{tr:b-n-y}}) field of building and continuation is only a supporting image, while the local sense remains filial. The repeated father-to-sons formula links this warning with 12:5 and 12:87, and the plural sons prepare the plural-gates strategy.

topics.headline: possessive filial address
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command is carried by Yaqub’s “my sons” relation, with plural sons already anticipating dispersed gates.
topics.reason: The possessive suffix and vocative are syntactically forced; building-root imagery is retained only as a secondary pressure, not as the local lexical sense.

words.gloss_range: prohibitive particle with jussive force
words.prose: {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}) is prohibitive: it does not merely describe non-entry, but blocks the specific pattern of entering from one gate. Its force sets the first half of the command pair, so the ayah begins by forbidding concentration before prescribing dispersion.

topics.headline: binding negative command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first instruction restrains a specific route before the ayah gives the permitted route.
topics.reason: The particle is lā al-nāhiya governing the jussive entry verb and scoping over one-gate entry.

words.gloss_range: prohibited entering, narrowed to one-gate entry rather than entry as such
words.root_gloss_range: entering into an interior, with broader exposure and inner-condition associations; here the concrete entry sense is selected under prohibition

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby referenced term or phrase used to preserve the local relation in prose

words.prose: {{ar:تَدْخُلُوا}} ({{tr:tadkhulū}}) carries the prohibition in its jussive form: the sons are not told to avoid entering altogether, but not to enter through one route. The {{ar:د خ ل}} ({{tr:d-kh-l}}) field keeps concrete movement into an interior, while the exposure/hidden-risk associations remain a narrowed pressure on why single-gate entry is dangerous. The same root returns positively in {{ar:ادْخُلُوا}} ({{tr:udkhulū}}), and 12:68 reports the sons’ entry as fulfillment.

topics.headline: jussive entry under prohibition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that entry itself is not rejected; only concentrated entry through one gate is made vulnerable and forbidden.
topics.reason: The verb is 2mp jussive under prohibitive {{ar:لَا}} ({{tr:lā}}), and the later imperative of the same root proves that only the manner of entry is negated.

words.gloss_range: preposition marking the route or entry point

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby referenced term or phrase used to preserve the local relation in prose

words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) ties the command to an entry-point: the issue is entering from a gate. By binding {{ar:بَابٍ}} ({{tr:bābin}}) to the verb, it makes the first route phrase the exact scope of the prohibition.

topics.headline: entry-point preposition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the danger is located in the route of entry, not in departure or travel generally.
topics.reason: The preposition governs {{ar:بَابٍ}} ({{tr:bābin}}) as the complement of the prohibited entry verb.

words.gloss_range: singular gate or access point in the prohibited route
words.root_gloss_range: door, gate, entrance, and by extension access or method; here the concrete gate sense leads, with method/access as controlled extension

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby referenced term or phrase used to preserve the local relation in prose

words.prose: {{ar:بَابٍ}} ({{tr:bābin}}) grounds the tactic in a concrete gate, an access point through which the brothers would become visible together. Its singular indefinite form is answered by {{ar:أَبْوَابٍ}} ({{tr:abwābin}}), so the local payoff is the singular/plural route contrast; the broader “method” sense is a controlled extension, not a replacement for the physical threshold. Earlier doorway scenes in Surah Yusuf sharpen the image of exposure (12:23; 12:25).

topics.headline: singular access point
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that one physical access point concentrates visibility and risk before the ayah opens multiple access points.
topics.reason: The noun is governed by {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) and modified by {{ar:وَاحِدٍ}} ({{tr:wāḥidin}}); method-language is retained only as an extension of the gate image.

words.gloss_range: adjectival numeral modifying the gate
words.root_gloss_range: oneness, aloneness, numerical one, and theological uniqueness; here it is a local adjective for a single gate, with theological contrast only by echo
words.prose: {{ar:وَاحِدٍ}} ({{tr:wāḥidin}}) modifies the gate and closes the prohibited route as “one gate.” The word forms the first pole of the ayah’s one-many antithesis against dispersed gates. Its echo with Joseph’s theological contrast between scattered lords and the One in 12:39 is real but narrowed: here the local force is tactical concentration, not a divine-name usage.

topics.headline: one-gate pole of antithesis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah’s local one-many contrast: one gate is tactically risky even as divine oneness remains the theological anchor elsewhere.
topics.reason: Agreement with {{ar:بَابٍ}} ({{tr:bābin}}) fixes the local adjectival sense; rows comparing divine oneness are kept as contrast, especially with 12:39, not as the direct meaning here.

words.gloss_range: coordinator linking prohibition to positive corrective command
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) joins the blocked route to its correction. It keeps the next command inside the same instruction unit: do not enter one way, but enter another way.

topics.headline: corrective coordination
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the positive command is the alternative to the prohibition, not a new scene.
topics.reason: The connector coordinates the positive command clause with the negative command clause.

words.gloss_range: direct imperative commanding distributed entry
words.root_gloss_range: entering into an interior; here the same action forbidden in one configuration is commanded in another
words.prose: {{ar:ادْخُلُوا}} ({{tr:udkhulū}}) restores entry as a direct command. The same {{ar:د خ ل}} ({{tr:d-kh-l}}) action moves from prohibited form to imperative form, so the ayah does not reject movement into Egypt; it requires a different configuration. The fulfillment reports in 12:68 and the later safe-entry scene in 12:99 keep this command operational.

topics.headline: positive entry command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same act of entering is restored as obedience once the route is changed.
topics.reason: The imperative shares the {{ar:د خ ل}} ({{tr:d-kh-l}}) root with the jussive prohibition and takes the same plural addressees.

words.gloss_range: preposition governing the plural gate phrase
words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) repeats the route frame from the prohibition, but now points to plural gates. The repetition makes the contrast exact: not from one gate, but from gates.

topics.headline: plural-route preposition
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same route grammar is reused, but now with multiple gates.
topics.reason: The second {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) governs {{ar:أَبْوَابٍ}} ({{tr:abwābin}}) and parallels the first route phrase.

words.gloss_range: plural gates or access points in the commanded route
words.root_gloss_range: door, gate, entrance, and access-method; here the plural concrete gates lead, with method/readiness as a controlled extension

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby referenced term or phrase used to preserve the local relation in prose

words.prose: {{ar:أَبْوَابٍ}} ({{tr:abwābin}}) answers the single {{ar:بَابٍ}} ({{tr:bābin}}) with multiple thresholds. The concrete plural gates carry the command’s tactic: spread the sons’ entry points so one spectacle does not form. A broader “approaches” sense can color the strategy, but the local grammar keeps physical route-language in front.

topics.headline: multiple access points
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the strategy shift from concentrated visibility to distributed thresholds.
topics.reason: The plural noun is governed by the second {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) and modified by {{ar:مُتَفَرِّقَةٍ}} ({{tr:mutafarriqatin}}); broader “methods” language remains secondary.

words.gloss_range: Form V active participle describing the plural gates as dispersed
words.root_gloss_range: separation, distinction, division, and discernment; here the selected sense is practical dispersal of gates, with broader furqan/discernment pressure only secondary
words.prose: {{ar:مُتَفَرِّقَةٍ}} ({{tr:mutafarriqatin}}) makes the plural gates actively dispersed. The feminine singular agreement fits the broken plural, while Form V gives the separation a marked texture: the commanded route is split apart on purpose. The echo with 12:39 is especially sharp because “scattered” is negative for lords there but practical wisdom for gates here.

topics.headline: self-dispersed separation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that dispersion is not disorder here; it is the commanded corrective to one-gate concentration.
topics.reason: Agreement with broken-plural gates fixes the adjective; links to {{ar:فُرْقَان}} ({{tr:furqān}}) and 12:39 are preserved as contrast without replacing local dispersal.

words.gloss_range: connector introducing the agency disclaimer
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) pivots from route-management to limitation. The same speech that gives a tactic immediately adds that the tactic does not control what comes from God.

topics.headline: from tactic to limit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Yaqub’s tactic is immediately checked by a statement of human inability.
topics.reason: The connector introduces the disclaimer clause after the two command clauses.

words.gloss_range: negative particle scoping over Yaqub’s availing power
words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) negates Yaqub’s ability to avail, not the sons’ obligation to act. After two commands, the particle makes clear that precaution is not sovereignty.

topics.headline: negated human efficacy
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Yaqub negates his own protective efficacy after commanding a practical precaution.
topics.reason: The particle negates {{ar:أُغْنِي}} ({{tr:ughnī}}), forming the disclaimer after the gate instructions.

words.gloss_range: Form IV availing or making sufficient, here negated absolutely
words.root_gloss_range: wealth, sufficiency, independence, and availing; here Form IV denies that Yaqub can make the sons sufficient against anything from God

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby referenced term or phrase used to preserve the local relation in prose
nearby referenced term or phrase used to preserve the local relation in prose
nearby referenced term or phrase used to preserve the local relation in prose

words.prose: {{ar:أُغْنِي}} ({{tr:ughnī}}) denies causative sufficiency: Yaqub cannot make his sons secure or avail them against anything from God. The first-person imperfect keeps the disclaimer personal and ongoing, while the chain {{ar:عَنْكُمْ}} ({{tr:ʿankum}}), {{ar:مِنَ اللَّهِ}} ({{tr:mina Allāhi}}), and {{ar:مِنْ شَيْءٍ}} ({{tr:min shayʾin}}) expands the denial to total scope. 12:68 repeats the availing language narratively.

topics.headline: causative sufficiency denied
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the father’s care is real but not efficacious against divine decree.
topics.reason: The 1sg imperfect is negated and followed by a layered prepositional stack; wealth/self-sufficiency imagery is narrowed to availing capacity.

words.gloss_range: preposition plus plural suffix naming those Yaqub cannot shield
words.prose: {{ar:عَنْكُمْ}} ({{tr:ʿankum}}) keeps the sons inside the disclaimer as the ones Yaqub cannot shield. The preposition gives the line a protective-separation shape: he cannot push anything away from them if it comes from God.

topics.headline: sons as protected party
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the disclaimer is still addressed to the sons Yaqub wants to protect.
topics.reason: The pronoun suffix is governed by {{ar:عَنْ}} ({{tr:ʿan}}) as complement of the availing verb.

words.gloss_range: preposition marking the divine source or domain against which Yaqub cannot avail
words.prose: {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) marks the domain from which Yaqub cannot protect them: from God. It turns the disclaimer from ordinary caution into a boundary of agency.

topics.headline: unbridgeable divine domain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the limit is not generic weakness but inability against what belongs to God’s domain.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the divine name in the disclaimer and frames the source of what cannot be averted.

words.gloss_range: proper divine name as the source-domain of what cannot be averted
words.root_gloss_range: the proper divine name, with worship/awe derivational fields in the background; here it names God as the source-domain before the sovereignty clause

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby referenced term or phrase used to preserve the local relation in prose
nearby referenced term or phrase used to preserve the local relation in prose

words.prose: {{ar:اللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) names the source-domain Yaqub cannot bridge. The first divine-name occurrence stands between the sons and the total object {{ar:شَيْءٍ}} ({{tr:shayʾin}}), then echoes into {{ar:لِلَّهِ}} ({{tr:lillāhi}}) in the judgment clause. That local echo also aligns Yaqub’s teaching with Joseph’s formula in 12:40.

topics.headline: divine name in agency limit
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the denial of Yaqub’s efficacy is already God-centered before the explicit judgment formula arrives.
topics.reason: The divine name is governed by {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) in the disclaimer and is repeated under {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) in the next clause.

words.gloss_range: augmentative preposition reinforcing negation

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby referenced term or phrase used to preserve the local relation in prose

words.prose: {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) is the small totalizing hinge before {{ar:شَيْءٍ}} ({{tr:shayʾin}}). Under negation, it makes Yaqub’s inability absolute rather than partial.

topics.headline: totalizing min
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the denial allows no smallest exception.
topics.reason: Under negation, the preposition before the indefinite noun reinforces total scope.

words.gloss_range: indefinite “thing” giving total scope under negation
words.root_gloss_range: thingness, object, matter, or anything conceivable; here the indefinite noun under augmentative {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) means no thing at all

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby referenced term or phrase used to preserve the local relation in prose

words.prose: {{ar:شَيْءٍ}} ({{tr:shayʾin}}) completes the total denial: not any thing. As an indefinite under augmentative {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}), it leaves no residual protective capacity for Yaqub, and 12:68 repeats the phrase as narrative confirmation.

topics.headline: anything under negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that no protective means, however small, is left outside the disclaimer.
topics.reason: The indefinite singular after augmentative {{ar:مِنْ}} ({{tr:min}}) under negation maximizes scope.

words.gloss_range: negative particle opening the exclusive restriction formula

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby referenced term or phrase used to preserve the local relation in prose

words.prose: {{ar:إِنِ}} ({{tr:ini}}) opens a compressed restriction: judgment is not anywhere except with God. The particle prepares the exclusive force that {{ar:إِلَّا}} ({{tr:illā}}) completes.

topics.headline: negation-exception restriction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the theological claim is framed as exclusivity, not merely preference.
topics.reason: The particle opens the negation side of the restrictive nominal clause completed by {{ar:إِلَّا}} ({{tr:illā}}).

words.gloss_range: definite verbal noun for judgment, rule, or governance
words.root_gloss_range: judging, ruling, restraining, deciding, and wisdom; here the definite verbal noun names the whole domain of judgment as restricted to God
words.prose: {{ar:الْحُكْمُ}} ({{tr:al-ḥukmu}}) names the domain that the restriction claims for God alone: judgment, ruling, and decisive governance. Its definiteness makes the claim institutional rather than one isolated decision. The word is the hinge between Yaqub’s inability disclaimer and the trust clauses, and the exact formula links father and son speech in 12:40 and 12:67.

topics.headline: restricted domain of judgment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah’s practical advice turns on a sovereignty claim: decision and rule belong only to God.
topics.reason: The definite maṣdar is the subject of an {{ar:إِنِ}} ({{tr:ini}})-{{ar:إِلَّا}} ({{tr:illā}}) clause; broader bridle/restraint imagery is retained only as root pressure.

words.gloss_range: exception particle completing the restriction
words.prose: {{ar:إِلَّا}} ({{tr:illā}}) completes the restriction. After the negative opening, it pivots the clause into exclusive assignment: judgment is not except for God.

topics.headline: exception completing exclusivity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the clause does not merely deny other judgment; it positively assigns judgment to God.
topics.reason: The exception particle completes the qaṣr construction begun by {{ar:إِنِ}} ({{tr:ini}}).

words.gloss_range: lām assigning judgment as belonging to God
words.prose: {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) makes the restriction possessive: the judgment belongs to God. The tiny preposition carries the clause from abstract theology into assignment of rightful ownership.

topics.headline: possessive assignment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that judgment is presented as belonging to God, not merely being performed by God.
topics.reason: The preposition governs the divine name as the restricted predicate of {{ar:الْحُكْمُ}} ({{tr:al-ḥukmu}}).

words.gloss_range: proper divine name as genitive possessor in the restriction
words.root_gloss_range: the proper divine name; here it names God as the exclusive owner of judgment

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby referenced term or phrase used to preserve the local relation in prose
nearby referenced term or phrase used to preserve the local relation in prose

words.prose: {{ar:اللَّهِ}} ({{tr:Allāhi}}) completes {{ar:لِلَّهِ}} ({{tr:lillāhi}}): judgment belongs to God alone. The second divine-name occurrence answers the first one in {{ar:مِنَ اللَّهِ}} ({{tr:mina Allāhi}}), moving from a limit on Yaqub’s power to a positive claim of divine ownership, while the prior oath scene in 12:66 remains in the background.

topics.headline: exclusive possessor of judgment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the divine name reappears as possessor after appearing as the source-domain no one can resist.
topics.reason: The divine name is governed by possessive {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) and completes the restricted predicate.

words.gloss_range: fronted prepositional complement of the trust verb

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby referenced term or phrase used to preserve the local relation in prose

words.prose: {{ar:عَلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhi}}) fronts the object of reliance before {{ar:تَوَكَّلْتُ}} ({{tr:tawakkaltu}}). The pronoun points back to God, so the clause begins with where trust is placed, not with Yaqub’s act. The “upon” image and reliance idiom stay together.

topics.headline: fronted object of trust
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the object of trust arrives before the act of trusting, subordinating strategy to God.
topics.reason: The pronoun resolves to God and the prepositional complement is syntactically required by the trust verb.

words.gloss_range: Form V perfect of reliance, first-person singular
words.root_gloss_range: delegating, appointing a trustee, relying, entrusting affairs, and sufficiency through another; here Form V selects self-entrusting reliance upon God
words.prose: {{ar:تَوَكَّلْتُ}} ({{tr:tawakkaltu}}) turns the sovereignty claim into Yaqub’s own completed act: “I have placed trust upon Him.” Form V keeps the self-entrusting force of the {{ar:و ك ل}} ({{tr:w-k-l}}) root, not generic optimism. It also answers the prior ayah’s divine trustee language in 12:66 and begins the ayah’s closing triplet: personal perfect, jussive command, and participial identity.

topics.headline: personal completed self-entrusting
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Yaqub’s strategy ends in a completed personal act of entrusting himself to God.
topics.reason: The Form V perfect has a first-person subject and required {{ar:عَلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhi}}) complement; weak/incapacity branches are not the local sense.

words.gloss_range: coordinator linking personal trust to communal command

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby referenced term or phrase used to preserve the local relation in prose

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) joins Yaqub’s personal trust declaration to the communal trust command. It makes the two {{ar:عَلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhi}}) clauses a pair rather than two detached endings.

topics.headline: personal-to-communal link
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that Yaqub’s personal trust is coordinated directly with a general command to trust.
topics.reason: The connector links {{ar:عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhi tawakkaltu}}) with the following {{ar:عَلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhi}})-fronted command clause.

words.gloss_range: second fronted prepositional complement with the same divine referent
words.prose: {{ar:عَلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhi}}) repeats the same fronted object of trust before the command. The repeated pronoun keeps God constant while the person shifts from “I trusted” to “let the trusters trust,” creating the local refrain of the tawakkul climax.

topics.headline: repeated fronted trust object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the universal command begins with the same object of reliance as Yaqub’s personal statement.
topics.reason: The second pronoun resolves to the same divine antecedent and supplies the complement of {{ar:يَتَوَكَّلِ}} ({{tr:yatawakkali}}).

words.gloss_range: consequential particle leading into the jussive command
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) makes the final command consequential. Because judgment belongs only to God and Yaqub has trusted Him, the speech now moves into an injunction for those who trust.

topics.headline: therefore into command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final command follows as a consequence of divine judgment and Yaqub’s trust.
topics.reason: The particle combines with lām al-amr before the jussive verb and marks the move from testimony to prescription.

words.gloss_range: jussive command lām forming an indirect imperative

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby referenced term or phrase used to preserve the local relation in prose
nearby referenced term or phrase used to preserve the local relation in prose

words.prose: {{ar:لْ}} ({{tr:l}}) is lām al-amr, the command marker that makes {{ar:يَتَوَكَّلِ}} ({{tr:yatawakkali}}) a third-person injunction. Joined to {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}), it compresses consequence and command into the recited cluster before the verb, and it opens the instruction beyond the sons to the named trusters.

topics.headline: third-person command marker
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the command broadens beyond the sons into a rule for the class of trusters.
topics.reason: The lām al-amr governs {{ar:يَتَوَكَّلِ}} ({{tr:yatawakkali}}), producing a third-person jussive injunction.

words.gloss_range: Form V jussive verb commanding reliance upon God
words.root_gloss_range: delegating, relying, entrusting affairs, and appointing a trustee; here Form V selects self-entrusting reliance in command mood

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: nearby referenced term or phrase used to preserve the local relation in prose
nearby referenced term or phrase used to preserve the local relation in prose

words.prose: {{ar:يَتَوَكَّلِ}} ({{tr:yatawakkali}}) is the conversion point: Yaqub’s completed {{ar:تَوَكَّلْتُ}} ({{tr:tawakkaltu}}) becomes a jussive command. The singular verb before a plural subject is normal verb-first grammar, and the fronted {{ar:عَلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhi}}) keeps the command fixed on God. The formula resonates with trust-command passages such as 9:51, 14:11, and the near-verbatim 14:12.

topics.headline: jussive self-entrusting command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices Yaqub’s completed trust becomes a commanded practice for trusters.
topics.reason: The verb is jussive under lām al-amr, takes the fronted {{ar:عَلَيْهِ}} ({{tr:ʿalayhi}}) complement, and precedes its plural subject in normal verb-first order.

words.gloss_range: definite Form V active participle naming the trusters
words.root_gloss_range: one who relies or commits affairs to another; here the definite plural participle names the class defined by reliance upon God
words.prose: {{ar:الْمُتَوَكِّلُونَ}} ({{tr:al-mutawakkilūna}}) closes the ayah by turning reliance into identity. The subject and command fold into each other: let the trusters trust. As a definite plural Form V active participle, the word completes the {{ar:و ك ل}} ({{tr:w-k-l}}) triplet from act to command to class, and it matches the near-verbatim closing formula in 14:12.

topics.headline: trust as named identity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah ends by naming a community through the very act it commands.
topics.reason: The participle is the explicit subject of the jussive verb; definiteness and Form V make the command name its own audience.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The prohibition of one gate, command of separated gates, denial of any power to avail, exclusive judgment, and repeated trust form one argumentative sequence.
baseline_models.mechanism: The father decomposes a shared exposure into several routes, then explicitly refuses to promote that diversification into sovereign causation. Practical agency remains real but bounded; outcome agency is recentralized in God.

activation_trace.role: The entryway image makes the one-versus-many contrast a concrete routing choice.
Union in one direction supplies the concentrated exposure that the prohibition breaks.
Scattering into parts performs the route diversification rather than dissolving the travelers' common purpose.
The sufficiency image makes the negation a refusal to treat the plan as adequate in God's place.
Judgment and decision identify the outcome-bearing level reserved to God.
Reliance completes the transfer of final outcome from route design to God.

changed_reading.before: A prudent father recommends separate gates and then adds a devotional qualification.
changed_reading.after: The ayah constructs a two-level causality: diversify what can be managed, then deny that managed exposure can substitute for God's decision.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The paired entry commands regulate movement at gates immediately before the claim that judgment belongs only to God.
baseline_models.mechanism: A human command can channel bodies at a threshold like a bridle channels motion, while lacking ownership of the event that follows. The apparent tension between precaution and trust becomes a distinction between local restraint and ultimate determination.

activation_trace.role: Literal ingress supplies the movement that the command locally regulates.
The limit or frontier image makes each gate a bounded control surface.
The bridle image renders judgment as restraint, distinguishing routed motion from ownership of its result.
Handing the affair over marks the boundary beyond the father's local direction.

changed_reading.before: The ayah juxtaposes practical precaution with a correction against fatal confidence.
changed_reading.after: The father's instruction is a legitimate bridle at the threshold, whereas God's judgment governs the unbridled remainder of the event.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The address to the sons places kinship directly beside the contrast between one route and separated routes.
baseline_models.mechanism: The sons are one built lineage whose parts are temporarily redistributed in space. Their unity is not abolished; it moves from bodily co-presence to a common object of reliance.

activation_trace.role: Filial descent supplies the literal unity of the addressed travelers.
Building by joining parts activates the family as a composite body.
A separated group supplies temporary spatial disassembly without loss of group identity.
Shared reliance preserves a non-spatial center for the dispersed family.

changed_reading.before: Several individual sons receive a travel-safety instruction.
changed_reading.after: A single kinship body is tactically disassembled across space and held together at a deeper level by common reliance.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: After separating the sons, the father moves from his own singular trust to an imperative addressed to all who trust.
baseline_models.mechanism: Spatial distribution could invite horizontal diffusion of responsibility. The repeated direct attachment to God prevents the separated agents from merely relying on one another until the affair is neglected.

activation_trace.role: Scattering supplies the condition in which responsibility could also become diffuse.
Mutual reliance that loses an affair supplies the failure mode excluded by direct reliance on God.
The repeated reliance language redirects every dispersed agent to the same dependable center.

changed_reading.before: The final repetition is devotional emphasis after a practical command.
changed_reading.after: The repetition is also an accountability design: dispersion must not become mutual deferral, so each agent relies directly on God.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier collective entrance produced an asymmetric recognition event: Joseph identified the brothers while they failed to identify him. Entering through separated gates can therefore be read as reducing the visible signature made by a conspicuous kin group, not only reducing generic physical exposure.

activation_trace.role: Union in one direction supplies the group configuration that can become a visible sign.
Scattering breaks the single configuration into less conspicuous units.
Recognition after a mark or trace makes group presentation an information-bearing exposure.
Non-recognition supplies the asymmetric informational field in which appearance management matters.

structural_cues: At 12:58 the brothers enter upon Joseph together, and recognition is one-way.
At 12:67 one-route entry is replaced by separated-route entry.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies collective entry and asymmetric recognition; I infer that group configuration can function as a recognizable mark; a live alternative is ordinary crowd or security management with no information-signature concern.

changed_reading.before: Different gates merely distribute a shared physical risk.
changed_reading.after: Different gates may also distribute a shared visual identity, managing how the brothers become legible as one group.

context_deltas.mechanism: Promises of guarding, remembered failed trust, a binding covenant, an exception for overwhelming enclosure, route diversification, and God as keeper form cumulative layers. Each human layer addresses a distinct failure mode while openly conceding catastrophic residual risk.

activation_trace.role: Spatial scattering adds a route-level control to the prior social controls.
Denied sufficiency prevents any layer from being treated as a guarantee.
The brothers' guarding promise supplies the first human protection layer.
Heart-security and trust expose the father's prior failed entrustment as a live risk memory.
The confirmed covenant formalizes responsibility beyond a verbal assurance.
Overwhelming enclosure names the residual catastrophe that defeats ordinary controls.
God as sufficient keeper places the layered precautions under a protection they cannot manufacture.

structural_cues: The father recalls an earlier failed entrustment and names God the better guardian at 12:64.
The covenant at 12:66 contains an explicit exception for being surrounded.
The route instruction at 12:67 immediately repeats the limit of human protection.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies successive guard, trust, covenant, catastrophe, routing, and divine-keeper elements; I infer a layered risk architecture; a live alternative is that these are adjacent reassurances without a designed hierarchy.

changed_reading.before: The separate-gates advice is one isolated precaution qualified by trust.
changed_reading.after: It is the route layer in a larger architecture of promise, covenant, catastrophe boundary, and divine keeping, with no layer mistaken for certainty.

context_deltas.mechanism: The following ayah both denies that the plan avails against God and affirms that it completes a need in Jacob's inner self, alongside attributed knowledge. The plan therefore succeeds in a bounded human domain while remaining powerless in the sovereign domain.

activation_trace.role: Denied sufficiency states precisely the domain in which the plan cannot stand in for God.
Exclusive decision reserves final outcome while leaving room for subordinate action.
Necessity and need identify the limited object that the instruction genuinely serves.

context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an unavailable royal-law route, an alternative penalty voiced by the brothers, divine strategy, and divine willing; I infer that sovereignty works by selecting among human procedural routes; a live alternative is a one-time legal exception unrelated to the focus gates.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it uses the non-dominant ق ل ل mapping under the focus root ق و ل and the fear branch of ف ر ق. It remains anchored to the father's spoken command and the explicit separated form, but downstream prose should present it only as an affective undertone, not as a replacement etymology for قال or متفرقة.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The father's act of saying and his command to separate can jointly carry a tremor-to-dispersion pattern.

activation_trace.role: The non-dominant mapped tremor image lets the spoken counsel register bodily instability beneath deliberate wording.
Fear that divides the heart projects that inner disturbance into the separated route pattern.

changed_reading.before: The father delivers calm logistical counsel and then qualifies it theologically.
changed_reading.after: The counsel may be disciplined speech spoken through tremor, externalizing a divided heart into a manageable geography.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This cross-domain reading is surprising because it links gates, a missing vessel, and searched containers through branch imagery rather than direct lexical identity. It remains anchored in the focus's one/many apertures and the later one-among-many search, but should be rendered as a formal narrative echo, not as proof that باب and صواع or وعاء are synonyms.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus distributes one company across many apertures; the later search distributes attention across many containers until one vessel reconcentrates the company around a single finding.

activation_trace.role: Making a thing into gates supplies the many-aperture architecture.
Scattering into parts establishes the outward movement later reversed by the search.
The vessel and measure image supplies the concrete missing object around which inquiry converges.
The same root's fracture and dispersion image echoes the company's earlier route separation.

changed_reading.before: The many gates are a one-time device for maintaining dispersion.
changed_reading.after: The gate pattern may prefigure a reversible aperture logic: distribution across many sites can later become the very field through which one concealed site is selected.

strongest_changes: The focus separates managed exposure from sovereign causation instead of opposing precaution and trust.
The surrounding pledge sequence turns the gate advice into one layer of a larger risk architecture with an explicit catastrophe boundary.
The next ayah confirms bounded efficacy: the plan completes an informed inner need while availing nothing against God.
The later legal sequence makes exclusive divine judgment procedural rather than abstract, routing an outcome through a human penalty that the royal order alone could not supply.
summary.what_was_special: The one/many gate contrast remained live across several domains: visual recognizability, family composition, affect regulation, selective reunion, and nested legal procedure. The reading changed most when the packet itself both denied control and affirmed completion, preserving human action without inflating it into sovereignty.
remaining_uncertainties: Recognition-signature management is structurally plausible but remains an inference rather than an explicit motive.
The completed need in Jacob may be affective relief, epistemic duty, practical prudence, or more than one of these at once.
The later vessel and container pattern may be a deliberate formal echo of the gates or only a productive cross-domain resonance.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Spatial dispersion is a precaution against concentrated visibility.** د خ ل B001, ب و ب B001, و ح د B002, and ف ر ق B002 turn one group into separated entry paths. I infer that distributing arrival reduces whatever risk attaches to conspicuous collective entrance. The precise hazard remains unstated, so the mechanism is cautious rather than predictive.
2. **Precaution is nested under non-sufficiency and delegated judgment.** غ ن ي B002 (availing), ح ك م B002, and و ك ل B001/B002 (handing over; reliance) explicitly deny that the tactic controls outcome. The ayah preserves planning and reliance as parallel layers.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 12:68 explicitly confirmed both sides: they followed the spatial plan, yet it did not independently avail them against God.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Doors as risk-distribution categories.** `ب و ب:B001` is an entrance; dormant `ب و ب:B002` is division into categories. The imperative divides one family group among multiple entrances, then immediately denies that this arrangement can avail against God; 12:68 confirms both their compliance and the strategy’s limited causal scope. The packet supplies spatial distribution and theological limit; I infer that separate doors reduce an ordinary concentrated exposure without guaranteeing outcome. The plural reads as practical categorization of risk, held beneath judgment rather than confused with it.

branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه قولهم دخل بامرأته كناية عن الإفضاء إليها.
يدخل فيه باطن الأمر والسريرة والدخلة والداخلة، وطرف الإزار الذي يلي الجسد، وما يطلع عليه من مكتوم الأمر.
يدخل فيه الدخل بمعنى العيب والفساد والدغل والريبة والمكر والخديعة والعداوة المستبطنة، وما وصف بمدخول لخلل في العقل أو الأصل أو الجوف أو الطعام.
يدخل فيه الدخيل والدخلل ومن يداخل الشخص في أموره، والقوم المنتسبون في غيرهم، والمتدخل المتكلف في الأمور.
يدخل فيه الدخل بمعنى مقابل الخرج، وما يدخل ضيعة الإنسان من المنالة.

branches.branch_image_ar: إدخال الإبل في الشرب مرة أخرى
branches.what_is_ar: يدخل فيه الدخال في الورد: أن ترد الإبل إلى الحوض ثانية أو يدخل بعير عطشان بين بعيرين ليتم شربه، وكذلك إيرادها عراكا في وجه آخر.
يدخل فيه مداخلة المفاصل، واللحمة المجتمعة على عصب، والدخلة في اللون، وريش ما بين الظهر والبطن، والكلأ الداخل في أصول الشجر.
يدخل فيه الدخل اسم الطائر الصغير، وجمعه دخاخيل أو دخاليل، مع تعليل دخوله بين الأشجار الملتفة.
يدخل فيه الدوخلة: سفيفة أو منسوج من خوص يجعل فيه الرطب.
